‘The video output circuit consists of three individual circuits; X axis, Y axis, and Z axis, video output circuits. The Z axis video output circuit consists of a shift register and a summer. X and ¥ Outputs The DACs (D11 and B11) each receive binary numbers from the vector generator’s posltion counters outputs. These numbers represent the location ofthe beam on the monitor. For the non-inverted X axi, the numbers range from 0 to 1023, where 0 is at the far lett of ‘the monitor screen, 512s atthe center, and 1023 is at the far right. For the nomvinverted Y_ axis, the numbers range from 128 to 996, where 128 is at the bottom of the monitor ‘screen, $12s atthe center, and 996s at the top. When the X axis and ¥ axis are inverted, ‘the monitor ploture Is turned upside down. This is used for a two-player cocktall game. ‘The DACs convert these binary number inputs to current outputs. The DACs’ current ‘outputs are applied to the pin 6 Inputs of current tovoltage converters C12 and A12. From the current-to-voltage converters, the signal is fed to two sampleand:hold cicuits: One is non-inverted and the other is inverted. The non-inverted sample and hold Consists of one stage of analog switch 012 and capacitor C9 for the X axis, and B12 and C108 for the Y axis. The inverting sample and hold consists of inverter E12, one stage of analog ewitch D12, and capacitor C119 for the X axis and B/C12, B12 and G118 for the Y

‘The sample and hold circuits are controlled by SHCON (sample and hold contro). ‘SHCON is derived by gating 3 MHz from the microcomputer clock circuitry and VGCK* trom the vector genorator’s state generator. The result of these inputs insures that the ‘non inverted and inverted analog signals that are applied to the analog switches have sutficiently stabilized before being applied to the sample and hold capacitors.

The output swing of SHCON Is 8 to +8 VDC. When SHCON is high, the voltage ccharges oF discharges the sampleand+hold capacitors to the X and Y analog voltage value. The voltages are then applied to the inputs of the second analog switch. These ‘Switches select elther the norinverted or inverted X-axis and Y-axis outputs. The outputs are then amplified by the second stages of C12 and A12 for an impedance:matched out put to the X and ¥ inputs to the monitor.
